Power good: the supply\'s voltages are steady
Standby: on whenever the supply is plugged in
Also +3.3 V\'s sense wire (brown) in many supplies
Pulled to ground, it switches the supply on
Not connected (−5 V in older supplies)
Sense: grounded, it tells the card the cable is in
ATX12V 2.x, as the plug\'s numbers read: 1–12 in one row, 13–24 in the other. The 20-pin plug is this without 11, 12, 23 and 24.
The CPU\'s EPS12V connector: grounds in one row, +12 V in the other. Don\'t mix it up with PCIe 8-pin.
A graphics card\'s power: 75 W through 6 pins, 150 W through 8
A graphics card\'s 16-pin plug, up to 600 W: +12 V in one row, ground in the other, the sideband pins under them. 12V-2x6 is 12VHPWR with shorter sense pins, so a plug not pushed home cuts the power.
The card says its power is good (optional)
The card sees the cable is in (optional)
With the other sense pin, grounded or open, tells the card its limit: both grounded 600 W, only SENSE1 450 W, only SENSE0 300 W, neither 150 W
The CPU\'s older 4-pin plug (P4): half of an EPS 8-pin, which it still fits
Staggered spin-up, or the drive\'s activity light
A drive\'s 15 contacts in a row; the five wires each feed three. Many cables leave out +3.3 V.
The 4-pin peripheral plug (AMP MATE-N-LOK): old drives, fans, LED strips
The small 4-pin Berg plug of floppy drives: Molex\'s voltages in the opposite order
